brief: Nvidia beat for a 17th straight quarter, guided Q4 revenue above consensus and raised fiscal 2028 growth to 75%, while Anthropic priced the largest IPO ever at a $1.5 trillion valuation: both catalysts bulls wanted. Stocks fell anyway, with the S&P down seven straight days, its worst week since Liberation Day, breaking its 200-day average. The causal chain: Anthropic's $107.3 billion raise pulled cash out of gold, bitcoin, copper and Nvidia to fund allocations, turning the IPO into a supply shock rather than a demand signal. Nvidia's new chair ruled out Jensen Huang's return and said the company would become more selective on customer financing, which Goldman reads as ending Nvidia's informal backstop role for AI spending. The Fed stayed hawkish (Waller's 50bp talk, hawkish October minutes) even as retail sales strength gave way to weak Empire, Philly Fed and UMich readings pointing to a slowdown. With hedge fund tech positioning near five-year lows and dealers running record short gamma, bonds, commodities and credit repriced toward growth risk while equities absorbed the move alone. Goldman's Privorotsky frames it as a 2018 repeat: the Fed overtightening into a market already under stress. The piece's own view: the bond market is right, the Fed will follow, but not before November CPI, so it treats rallies as ones to sell until then.
